text: Beginner path, in order: decide a name, buy the domain, learn where DNS records go, then connect sending (Resend + Supabase), receiving (ImprovMX + Gmail), DMARC and testing. Open each task's Step-by-step guide below. Full reference doc: https://claude.ai/artifact/DKKUaRRwxsnpbCCqNZarJ3. Vercel Hobby is fine while the app is free; move to Pro before charging. Replace yourdomain.com everywhere with your real domain.
Decide your domain name and set up a place to keep passwords
details:
Pick 3 short name ideas (easy to spell, no hyphens, ideally .com) and check they are not another company's brand.
Set up a password manager (search: Bitwarden free) or a private note. You will create about 6 logins and 2 API keys in this section.
Save every login and key there the moment you create it.
Tip: Use one dedicated email address for all these accounts, for example a new Gmail just for your business.

text: Buy the domain on Vercel and attach it to your project (SSL is automatic)
details:
Go to vercel.com and log in (or sign up; Continue with GitHub is the quickest).
In the dashboard click Domains in the top menu.
Use the search box to type the name you want, for example myapp.com, and press Search.
Check the first-year price and the renewal price before paying. Avoid names marked premium that cost hundreds.
Add a payment card and complete the purchase. Keep auto-renew on so you do not lose the domain.
Open your project, go to Settings, then Domains, click Add Domain, enter your domain and confirm. Wait for a green Valid Configuration.
Open https://yourdomain.com in the browser. You should see your site with a padlock. HTTPS is automatic, so do not buy SSL anywhere.
Search: Vercel buy domain, Vercel add domain to project
Tip: Vercel's menus change sometimes. If you cannot find a button, use the search box at the top of the dashboard.

text: Find the DNS Records page in Vercel (you will use it in every step below)
details:
In Vercel click Domains in the top menu.
Click your domain name.
Open the DNS Records section and click Add. You will see fields: Name, Type (A, CNAME, MX or TXT), Value, and Priority for MX.
Tip: In Name, type only the part before your domain. For resend._domainkey.yourdomain.com enter resend._domainkey. For the main domain itself leave Name empty (or @ if asked).
Tip: Copy and paste values exactly. A missing character or extra space is the most common reason verification fails.
Warning: DNS changes can take a few minutes up to a few hours to take effect.
Search: Vercel add DNS record

text: Add the domain in Resend and paste its DKIM/SPF records into Vercel DNS
details:
Go to resend.com, click Sign up (free) and confirm your email.
In the left menu click Domains, then Add Domain.
Type your domain (yourdomain.com). If asked for a region, choose the one closest to your users.
Resend now shows a table of DNS records (usually TXT and MX). Keep this tab open.
In another tab open Vercel, Domains, your domain, DNS Records. Add each record from the table, copying Type, Name and Value exactly. For MX records also copy the Priority.
Back in Resend click Verify DNS Records. The status becomes Verified (a few minutes to a few hours).
Tip: Do not delete records Vercel already created for your website.
Search: Resend verify domain

text: Create two Resend API keys (one for Supabase, one for Gmail)
details:
In Resend click API Keys in the left menu, then Create API Key.
Name it supabase-auth, set Permission to Sending access, and choose your domain.
Click Add and copy the key immediately (it starts with re_). Resend shows it only once.
Save it in your password manager.
Repeat to create a second key named gmail-support. You will use it in the Gmail step.
Warning: Never paste an API key into your website code or push it to GitHub. Anyone with it can send email as you.

text: Enter Resend SMTP in Supabase (smtp.resend.com / 465 / user resend / API key as password)
details:
Go to supabase.com/dashboard and open your project.
In the left sidebar click Authentication.
Open Emails, then the SMTP Settings tab. If you cannot find it, use the dashboard search box for SMTP. Older dashboards have it under Project Settings, Authentication.
Turn on Enable custom SMTP.
Fill in: Sender email no-reply@yourdomain.com, Sender name your app name, Host smtp.resend.com, Port 465, Username resend, Password the supabase-auth API key.
Click Save changes.
Tip: The sender email must use the domain you verified in Resend, or the emails will be rejected.
Search: Supabase custom SMTP Resend

text: Set Supabase Site URL and redirect URLs; customise the email templates
details:
In Supabase go to Authentication, then URL Configuration.
Set Site URL to https://yourdomain.com.
Under Redirect URLs click Add URL and add https://yourdomain.com/** . For local testing also add http://localhost:3000/** (use your own dev port).
Save. Then go to Authentication, Emails, Templates.
Open Confirm sign up, Reset password and Magic link one by one. Change the subject and wording to match your app.
Keep the link placeholder in each template (for example {{ .ConfirmationURL }}) exactly as it is, or the link will break.
Warning: A wrong Site URL makes confirmation links open the wrong website.

text: Create the support@ alias in ImprovMX and add its MX + SPF records
details:
Go to improvmx.com and sign up (free plan).
Enter your domain and continue.
Create an alias: type support and set it to forward to your Gmail address. A catch-all (*) is optional.
ImprovMX shows the records to add: two MX records and one TXT (SPF). The MX values are normally mx1.improvmx.com (priority 10) and mx2.improvmx.com (priority 20).
In Vercel DNS Records add both MX records (Name empty, Type MX, the Value, the Priority) and the TXT record.
Back in ImprovMX click Check DNS until the records show a green tick.
Tip: A domain can have only one SPF record. If a TXT starting with v=spf1 already exists on the main domain, merge both into one line instead of adding a second.
Tip: Resend's records usually sit on a subdomain, so they do not clash with these.
Search: ImprovMX setup Vercel

text: Set up Gmail Send mail as for support@ using Resend SMTP
details:
Open Gmail in a computer browser (not the phone app) and click the gear icon, then See all settings.
Open the Accounts and Import tab. Next to Send mail as click Add another email address.
Enter Name (for example MyApp Support) and Email support@yourdomain.com, then Next Step.
Choose Send through SMTP server: Server smtp.resend.com, Port 465, Username resend, Password the gmail-support API key, Secured connection using SSL. Click Add Account.
Gmail sends a confirmation email to support@yourdomain.com. Thanks to ImprovMX it lands in your Gmail inbox. Click the link or enter the code.
When writing a new email click the From line and choose support@yourdomain.com. Replies automatically use the address the message was sent to.
Warning: If Gmail shows an error, re-check the API key and that your domain is Verified in Resend.
Search: Gmail send mail as custom SMTP

text: Add the _dmarc TXT record
details:
In Vercel go to Domains, your domain, DNS Records, then Add.
Type TXT, Name _dmarc, Value v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:you@gmail.com (use your real email).
Save. p=none only monitors and blocks nothing while you test.
Check it: search MXToolbox DMARC lookup, enter yourdomain.com and confirm the record appears.
Tip: After a few weeks with no problems you can tighten the policy to p=quarantine.

text: Test signup / password reset / magic link end to end
details:
From your personal email send a message to support@yourdomain.com. It should reach Gmail within a minute.
Reply from support@ using the From dropdown and confirm the reply arrives.
On the received reply click the three dots, then Show original. SPF, DKIM and DMARC should all say PASS.
Sign up in your app using a different email address. Confirm the email arrives from no-reply@ and is not in spam.
Test Reset password and Magic link too. Click each link and confirm it opens your real domain.
Optional: search mail-tester, send a test email to the address it gives you and aim for 8/10 or higher.
Tip: If an email does not arrive, check Resend, Emails (logs) and Supabase, Authentication, Logs.

text: Idea: bank and UPI alert emails are forwarded to a dedicated address (for example track@yourdomain.com). An inbound-email webhook calls a Supabase Edge Function that extracts amount, date and merchant and saves a pending transaction for you to confirm. Check that your email provider offers inbound email on its free plan before building. Privacy: store only the parsed fields, not the full email body, and tell users clearly what is read. Start with one bank format, then add others.
Collect 5-10 real alert emails from one bank/UPI app (hide personal details) as test samples
Create the receiving address and point inbound mail to a webhook
Write a Supabase Edge Function that parses amount / date / merchant / debit-credit
Save results as pending transactions with a Confirm / Edit / Reject screen
Verify the sender and add a per-user secret so strangers cannot inject transactions
Write a Gmail filter guide so users can auto-forward only their bank alerts

Easiest hybrid route: wrap your existing web app with Capacitor, so one codebase serves web and Android. Google Play needs a one-time developer registration fee. New personal developer accounts usually must run a closed test with a group of testers for about two weeks before production access; check Google's current rules before planning dates. Build the app as a responsive PWA first.

Test on a real phone: login, deep links for email confirmation

Apply for production access and publish
Start where people already complain about spreadsheets. Talk to 10 people before you write more code. Track every conversation in a simple list (name, channel, feedback, follow-up date).
Write a one-line pitch and define your first target group (students / freelancers / households)
Message 20 people you know and ask how they track money today
Join 3-5 relevant communities (Reddit finance subs, Telegram/WhatsApp groups) and help before promoting
Build a simple landing page with a waitlist form

Ask each happy user for one referral and one testimonial
Review weekly: signups, active users, feedback themes

Do this only with real paying customers and a clear reason (cost, compliance, scale). Supabase is Postgres, so your data can move with pg_dump. The harder parts are auth, row-level security rules, storage and edge functions, which you must replace (for example RDS or Aurora for the database, Cognito for auth, S3 for files, Lambda for functions). Consider upgrading Supabase to its paid plan first; it is usually far less work than a migration.
Define the trigger: for example 50+ paying users, or a limit you keep hitting
List every Supabase feature you use (auth, RLS, storage, realtime, functions)
Try the paid Supabase plan before deciding to leave
Build the AWS copy in staging and test a pg_dump restore
Plan the cutover: announce downtime, take a final backup, switch DNS and keys
